content.title: HAPPY APRIL FOOL'S DAY! 🇯🇵 Pearl Jam just announced 檸檬色の太陽 (Lemon Yellow Sun)! - pearljamonline.it
content.text: 𝗨𝗣𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗘: The owls are not what they seem… and every April 1st, the pearljamonline.it April Fools’ prank always shows up After announcing the reissue of the official bootleg Live in Budokan, the Japan edition of Earthling, and after dropping several Pearl Jam videos on YouTube with Japanese subtitles, the band just surprised fans with something totally unexpected. With Eddie Vedder heading out on his first-ever solo tour in Japan, the band is rolling out a special release: 10 of the most iconic Pearl Jam songs… completely re-recorded in Japanese. Yeah, you read that right. On this new collection Vedder sings every lyric in Japanese, while the rest of the band trades their usual gear for traditional Japanese instruments: Jeff Ament on koto Stone Gossard on shamisen Mike McCready on shakuhachi Holding it all together is a powerful Japanese Taiko Loop Station drum machine, creating atmospheric soundscapes inspired by the vibe of Lost in Translation. TRACKLIST 檸檬色の太陽 / LEMON YELLOW SUN 1. Alive – アライヴ 2. Even Flow – イーブンフロー 3. Black – ブラック 4. Jeremy – ジェレミー 5. Better Man – ベター・マン 6. Yellow Ledbetter – イエロー・レッドベター 7. Daughter – ドーター 8. Corduroy – コーデュロイ 9. Given to Fly – ギヴン・トゥ・フライ 10. Wishlist – ウィッシュリスト The project blends classic Pearl Jam energy with traditional Japanese instrumentation, promising a totally fresh and unexpected listening experience — what Vedder reportedly called “real Japanese spirit in the mix.” Release details Label: Ten Club Japan Catalog #: SICP-6589 Total running time: 42:17 Format: Japan-exclusive CD release The disc will be pressed on CD only and available today only at supermarkets across Japan. And there’s more: the bonus track is a Japanese-language cover of Hurt by Nine Inch Nails featuring a very special guest — Ken Jeong (yep, Leslie Chow from The Hangover trilogy). Fun fact from the sessions: according to the band, the hardest song to pronounce in Japanese was still Yellow Ledbetter. As an old Japanese saying goes: 猿も木から落ちる Even monkeys fall from trees.
